channel.description: Software Developer. Luddite. Cat and Dog friend.

item.title: Lessons Learned: None
item.content:encoded:
I found a picture of all of us. Of you, of me, of everybody in society. Here, take a look.

The first time around

Remember when social media didn’t feel like the addictive drug it feels like today? It promised to connect us to the people in our communities and to open the doors to connecting with people in disparate places that once-upon-a-time seemed so inaccessible.

There was a genuinely lovely feeling associated with logging on or in to whatever platform and seeing what was going on. Getting nudged, poked, or seeing an alert pop up weren’t the exhausting mental hurdles they seem to be today.

Facebook kind of made sense at the time. My friends posted pictures of the things they wanted to share, the stuff we did together, the stuff I missed out on. It was a place where groups were formed and events were planned. That was kind of it, and it was enough. Or wait, they added games too at some point. Okay, that’s fine I guess; some of the games are literally just online gambling which is a bit weird but okay. Oh, also it started showing us stuff from people we didn’t know at all and weren’t connected to. Hmm, I don’t get it, but maybe some people made new friends?

As it got bigger, something else started to happen; it became a source for news and information in a way we never really imagined in the early days. If someone had told me when I first got on there that this is where a significant number of people would get their news one day, I legitimately would not have understood what you meant. The place that my friend posted the pictures he took of us smoking cigarettes outside of school that we had to comment on frantically because he had made them public so everyone could see them and that meant that someone might tell my parents PLEASE TAKE THIS OFF OR MAKE IT PRIVATE YOU FUCKER!?!

That place?

Well, apparently 40% of Americans get their news from Facebook and YouTube, check it out. (I don’t mean to pick on Americans, I’m sure this is representative of a majority of the world. It’s just the data I found after a quick search).

Okay, so people are getting their news and information from Facebook, surely this company will build systems to manage this in a responsible way? Right?

OH FUCKING HELL. Crimes against humanity? Ethnic cleansing? BY THE FUCKING PLATFORM THAT LET YOU POKE YOUR FRIENDS?

Okay, we all get it now

Okay, yeah social media went off the rails. The companies that built these things started building power and in the relentless pursuit of mARkEt SHaRe, they acquired smaller social media firms just as those companies got interesting and fun. The more users on your infernal poke machine, the more eyeballs you could guarantee on an ad; and so advertising became the entire thing. Acquiring more firms became the easiest way to get more users into your ’ecosystem.’ And we the people, the people who just wanted to go to parties and share our holiday photos? We became the product. The advertisers and the social media giants traded us like whatever it is that kids trade these days.

The conspiracy theories, the calls to violence, the naked racism, the hatred, all of those became features. That’s the stuff that keeps people coming back to the platform.

These stupid companies have become behemoths and they think they can do everything because they made a website where you and your friends can write messages to each other. For the most part people are awake to this, and we’re aware of the extreme damage that social media has done to us as individuals and to our societies. We’ve given these firms far too much power, and we’ve let our brains deteriorate by the power of doomscroll.

This will never happen again!

I’ll fucking do it again

If you’ve read my blog before then you knew it was just a matter of time before I turned my rambling towards the looming spectre of so called AI.

It’s happening again; in different ways and also in the same ways. New corporate behemoths (and some of the same old ones) have risen to offer us a new toy. This toy is going to change everything!

Sometimes they say it will bring about abundance! (THE AUTOMATIC DICTIONARY MACHINE WILL BRING ABOUT ABUNDANCE EVERYBODY)

Other times they tell us it will destroy everybody! (THE AUTOMATIC DICTIONARY MACHINE WILL DESTROY US ALL)

The words don’t matter; everything they say, they say to get us to use the machine. This time I’m approaching it with the perspective of someone who has been through one civilizational paradigm shift already, and I’m not going in with the naive optimism I had when I was 17.

First off, I will acknowledge that the LLM’s are good at stuff. They are great at coding, that’s my expertise so I’ll stop there. I’ve heard they can be useful for maths (though there is debate around whether we are losing track of what makes maths research useful). There, I said it, it can be useful.

With respect to so called AI in art, music, literature, and the things that make life wonderful, this is just fucking stupid in my opinion. Even if they are “good” at these things, the point of art, the whole fucking point of any art is not just to produce an artifact. The universe flows through the experiences of an individual human being. That person interprets this experience and does…something with it. It comes out as music, as a painting, as a book, as a recipe, as a new football trick. The point of art is to experience, interpret, present to others, and for them to ingest and re-interpret. The LLM is not a conscious human, whatever it does is irrelevant in this field.

Anyway, back to the point. We are once again hurtling head-first to a world in which a handful of corporations are very openly trying to control us by controlling the means of production very much like the social media companies did. Except it is much worse this time. When mass produced LLM bullshit meets social media echo chambers, we are at levels of fucked that we’ve never seen before. Of course, it’s happening already.

Also, and perhaps more insidious, the fake claims that these so called AI CEO guys are making about abundance and changing work point towards their true intentions. They want to sell a product that replaces workers, because the one thing that a capitalist needs is the working class, and there is nothing they’d like to shed more than the working class. If they can create these stupid automatic working machines, they won’t need the working class anymore; amazing! At the very least they will have massively undermined the working class by reducing its ability to negotiate, by making the individuals more replaceable, all to capture even more value than they already are. No one knows what it means if no one on earth at that point will be able to afford anything, who cares? Workers are consumers too, what happens when workers can’t consume? ¯_(ツ)_/¯

Something that concerns me specifically is their control over the actual physical means of production. With social media we already had to contend with this; the corporations owned the servers and therefore our data. This is much worse with the so called AI guys. They own the data centres where the inference happens, we have to rent inference time from them. Like I said, I acknowledged that the things are good at some types of work, but I do not want to live in a world in which I am dependent on a third party’s goodwill to get my work done. I do not want to pay a subscription for a service that I so intimately dependent on, that can be turned off or changed without my input. This isn’t the same as paying netflix or spotify or whatever, this is paying for something that they are telling you to use to replace your brain with for your work.

You are supposed to depend on this thing; how do I do that when I have no control over it? Oh, just run a local model. Really? These assholes have made it so expensive to build a PC because they’ve destroyed the supply chain, and now they’re telling us that actually this is a good thing!

Why I’m concerned

I’m thinking about this because I have begun to perceive a cognitive dissonance in people. Most people, I think, will agree with the premise that social media has negatively impacted society and that regulation is very badly required.

Some people do feel this way about so called AI as well, but for the most part people are very cheerfully walking right in without questioning the tool, the technology, or the corporations providing them to us. Can they do things that make your life easier? Yes. Should we just give in and let them do all the stuff then? I reject that. Social media took over our social lives. It has dramatically reduced the quality of our friendships and other relationships, and we’re not better off with it, I very strongly believe this. So called AI goes further. It is not the same, but it will accentuate and accelerate the social isolation that people feel. Why even have friends when you can chat with a robot that will always tell you you’re amazing? But beyond that, what it is made to do is to reduce your ability to participate in the economy. This is catastrophic for both, the individual and for society. What happens when people lose their ability to make money, and to contribute to society? And what happens when the economy is no longer built by people, but by machines that are given their mandate by a handful of sociopaths?

I think we need to slow down and ask questions about how to regulate these things. I’m not saying this as one of those doomers that think that the so called AI is going to download itself into a robot body and come for me like a T1000; I’m talking about this from the perspective of someone who has seen what happened to us in the 2010’s and early 2020’s. It was a slow, insidious take over of the social lives of people and we’re still struggling with the fallout. This is happening again and we need to engage with it with that level of seriousness.

item.title: Escalators
item.description: Krist Novoselic on the AI brainrot
item.content:encoded:
I love this rant. In this video, Krist Novoselic goes off on escalators. Specifically the way that people use them. Watch it.

In case you didn’t actually watch, his rant is about how escalators were designed like stairs because they’re meant to be used like them. They just make us faster at going up stairs. Krist Novoselic is frustrated by people standing on escalators.

Things that I love about the video:

  • How stoned he is.
  • How Kurt and Dave immediately groan as he begins the rant. This is obviously a recurring theme.
  • Kurt butts in with a solution. Stand to the side so that people can walk up the left. Krist ignores him and continues the rant.

I found this on YouTube years ago, I watched it, and then forgot about it. The stupid AI bullshit in the air these days reminded me that it existed.

Excuse me, whatever the fuck do you mean?

What I mean is that so called “AI” is the Escalator. I’m just going to ignore the fact that what is referred to as a monolithic AI is actually a myriad set of technologies. LLM’s have taken over the concept and when people say AI now they kind of just mean one of these LLM’s. Whatever, I’m just going to say AI and you, the reader, can substitute whatever you want in there.

What matters is the idea. AI is supposed to make us better and quicker but people are standing on the escalator. Instead of being better and quicker, we’re feeding things into the machine and regurgitating what it tells us.

I’m sure there are people that are like “oh man I don’t use it that way, I have a workflow that blah blah blah blah.” Great, neat. I’m not talking about you.

I’m talking about:

  • The people inundating YouTube with generated music playlists
  • The people wasting everyone’s time with generated emails
  • The ‘grok, is this true?’ morons on twitter
  • Other similar people doing similarly idiotic things

People don’t care about being better, they just care about quicker. In fact, quicker and shittier is fine.

I’ll admit, after having gotten this far into writing this, the analogy does seem to break down a bit. We’re not all trying to go to the same place and so we’re not all standing on the same escalator. Some people are all about the hustle and grind and other people are normal. My point is that the way so called AI is being marketed to us is the same way the escalator was probably sold to people, i.e. “wow, we are about to accelerate into the future!” But we actually end up going slower. I’m also aware that part of the benefit of an escalator is to be able to rest your legs. And if that’s what you want to do, rest your brain, that’s cool.

To me, Krist’s rant sounds almost prophetic, like he was possessed by someone from the future. You want to stand on the escalator? Fine, let me take the stairs or go some other way. I don’t have to stand on this thing with you. Which leads me to the next point.

The “AI is inevitable” bullshit

There’s a lot of this going around right now. Posts where people try to convince you that “AI is here now and you need to adapt” are basically the main genre of things being uploaded to LinkedIn. “AI won’t take your job, a person using AI will.”

Shut. The. Fuck. Up.

None of this is inevitable. Megacorps (run by loser finance guys posing as scientists) have been given the keys to our societies and are engaging in wildly unethical, unsustainable extractivism. These posts about inevitability and people having to adapt are just attempts to manufacture consent. We don’t have to accept anything or adapt to anything if we don’t want to, especially if it is harmful to people.

And sure, call me a Luddite. I don’t mind. In fact I consider it a badge of honour.

Everything is business, nothing is interesting

I actually happen to think this stuff is interesting. LLM’s are cool. Computer Vision is cool. Machine Learning is cool. But the CEO’s, VP’s of Sales, Heads of Marketing, etc are hell-bent on pushing this shit on us as a foRcE mULtIpLIeR.

There are great applications for these kinds of technologies. Here’s an incredible example. The indigenous Māori language, te reo Māori, is dying. The goal of Te Hiku Media is to collect all the recorded te reo Māori that they can find and build a model for the language. They are currently able to translate between te reo Māori and English with 82% accuracy.

All of this was done with the Māori peoples’ consent and participation. They used two GPU’s to get the model trained. And the tool has been built to do something specific. When these tools use data that makes sense for a specific job, not only can they produce amazing results, but they can be trained to do so without chugging infinite amounts of fresh water, producing noise pollution, emanating waves of heat, and crashing global supply chains because of chip hoarding. Te Hiku Media exists in opposition to the fucking Silicon Valley ethos which seems to involve taking whatever they want from whomever they want without asking for permission.

And the problems they claim they are trying to solve are…¯\(ツ)/¯

Listening to these weirdos talk about it is crazy. Apparently it doesn’t make sense to focus on climate change because it’s too hard, we should just create a digital god to solve the problem for us.

Wut?

Oh and the god is hungry. The god needs to eat tens of thousands of GPU’s to generate images cobbled together from art made by real people so that LinkedIn losers can write a post about #marketing.

It gets worse

Just the fact that we are watching a handful of people burn the atmosphere for social media clicks is dire enough, but it does actually get worse than that.

So called “AI” is being used to murder people in an ongoing genocide.

If you’re one of those people that thinks posting Al Jazeera makes me a woke radical or whatever then here’s another source, actually the original source. Though I know that if you think Al Jazeera is woke then +972 will be as well for you.

We’ve known for a long time that the megacorps have been collecting all our data. Sometimes with our consent and often without. Google, Microsoft, Netflix, Facebook/Meta, Twitter, Apple, Amazon, etc; they’re all constantly sucking up whatever they can from us under the protection of the commercial relationships we have signed up for under them. But they’re doing worse things than just that bullshit. Microsoft has been storing surveillance data on their cloud. This is the data collected from a people living under occupation.

Similarly Google has ‘Project Nimbus’, which provides cloud storage and compute to the IOF. I wonder what they use it for? Surely just to store HR/payroll documents.

And then there’s the next level of evil tech assholes. Personally I think that the New York Times is a neo-liberal rag but here’s something that they wrote that should be read. Peter Thiel backed Palantir is building a domestic panopticon, the elusive surveillance state that the Republicans have been trying to create since the early 2000’s.

This is scary, fucked up shit. And it is directly related to the stupid fucking Studio-Ghibli-stealing-image-generator-machines. These are the same thing, they come from the same place, from the same minds, from the same venture capital money.

Krist Novoselic tried to warn us.

Recommended brain reset tools

  • Empire of AI. Brilliant. The first time I heard the story about Te Hiku Media was actually on the podcast, Tech Won’t Save Us (Paris Marx), but reading about it again in Empire of AI recently made me think about how this stuff can be wonderful. And how like many technologies, it is being co-opted by lunatics.

  • Tech Won’t Save Us. My favourite podcast. Always fantastic guests, and always great conversation about what is happening. It’s not an “oh shit things are hopeless” vibe either. It’s always presenting a hopeful vision.

  • DAIR. Timnit Gebru was fired from Google for doing her job well. i.e. researching the ethical implications of AI (specifically for co-authoring this paper on LLM’s). She is one of the great researchers that went on to found DAIR, an independent institute that explores a better vision for technology.

  • Where’s Your Ed At. Ed Zitron’s very funny blog. His piece on business idiots is just fantastic.

  • Nik Suresh. I’ve linked to a specific post that killed me the first time I read it, but Nikhil’s blog is amazing in general.

item.title: This is the Anti-Rant that Never Ends
item.description: I will keep updating this with things that delight me.
item.content:encoded:
After hearing about my rant post, Geetha suggested I do one for things that delight me. I think it’s a good idea, there are a lot of things that make me happy and it’ll be nice to jot them down over time.

July 12, 2025

  • The way Gobi (my dog) sighs and burrows her head into the bed as she makes herself comfortable, ready to nap.
  • Software that is built by people for other people and not for “customers.” Things like jellyfin, mealie, and freshRSS.
  • Community building. This is kind of wishy-washy but it means something different to everyone. I know it when I see it and I love it. The neighbourhood I live in always has something happening, especially in the summer. Also my neighbours are lovely in general and it really feels like people care about each other. This is a great resource for more concrete examples of real things happening in Toronto.
  • Cycling. It feels like freedom.

February 23, 2026

  • PROPAGANDHI!!!!! Best. Canadian. Band. Ever. They have dethroned Rush (for me) and my biggest regret is getting into them so late. There are so many things that I love about them:
    • Their politics are progressive, inclusive, radical, and energizing. It feels so good to engage with music that is so unapologetically true to these values, especially when everything around us is melting to the ground and the overwhelming response seems so milquetoast and subsumed by corporate enshittification.
    • They have evolved with every album and even though I do like that old 90’s punk sound, I love the thrashy metal sound they’ve grown into. That’s actually more my speed.
    • The songs aren’t conventional at all. They’re not verse-chorus-verse-chorus-bridge-verse or whatever. They’re full of time changes, poetic streams of consciousness, and stank-face riffage.
    • They are just fucking awesome.

item.title: This is the Rant that Never Ends
item.description: I will keep updating this with things that piss me off.
item.content:encoded:
There’s a lot in this world that makes me mad. When something like this is actively on my mind I’ll try to add it to this list instead of letting it occupy my thoughts. Maybe this will be helpful. Some of these things are probably bigger than others.

July 12, 2025

  • The religious zealotry around whatever the contemporary hotness coming out of silicon valley is. There is almost no critical thought around what, why, how, and for whom, and a lot of fawning over “growth”, “value”, and other such metrics.
  • People that fight to “preserve the character of their neighbourhoods.” This is almost always NIMBYs fighting to keep other people out of a home and to deny efficient, equitable transit to those that rely on it. Usually this is for the sake of their “property values” but can sometimes be for even stupider reasons like not wanting to lose a parking spot.
  • Food delivery apps that claim to be innovative when their actual accomplishments include:
    • Cannibalizing our municipal infrastructure for their own use without contributing to upkeep in any meaningful way
    • Turning the employment relationship on its head and exploiting people as a result
    • Delivering an inferior version of good food for the low price of ${extremelyExpensive}.
  • People that walk really slowly on the sidewalk while also blocking the way for everyone behind them. Take your time but please let me get by.

September 21, 2025

  • People that like living in unwalkable, pedestrian hostile, boring suburbs acting like they should have not just a say in the urban planning and development of my city, but the final word. Our own authoritarian provincial leader kowtowing to this selfish cohort so that he can keep power like the No Name dictator that he is makes this beyond infuriating.

  • This recent push to return to the office for PrOdUcTivITy. No research to back it up, no explanation besides “it is better”, “duh watercooler chats”, etc. Our cities are less congested now, people have better lives now, our salaries mean more now. But sure, change it all for the vibes you goddamn ghouls.

February 24, 2026

  • People fawning over LLMs. Sorry, this is kind of the same as the one from July but it really fucking annoys me. There’s so much trash on LinkedIn about “WOW THE AI DID AN AMAZING THING” with very little substance behind it. I have connections that are constantly commenting on posts about how useful the LLM they love is, but there’s no github repos, no deployed applications, no ideas being discussed, no nothing. Just a bunch of circle-jerking, self-aggrandizing posts that mean next to nothing. I actually think that the stupid AI tools are kind of useful sometimes, but in the same way as many other tools that I’ve used. I’m not fucking slithering around LinkedIn commenting on various posts about how AMAZING my calculator is because it SAVED ME SO MUCH TIME or whatever. I don’t fucking care that a fucking language model saved you 4 minutes you fucking weirdos. SoFTwArE iS CoOKEd, this is that, that is this. Fucking stupid assholes.

item.title: Public Service Announcement
item.content:encoded:
I do a lot of things that are ultimately meaningless but make me feel good. One of these things is getting good bread instead of the supermarket stuff. This means getting bread from bakeries and cafes near us instead of the Dempsters and Villagio. However, due to the convergence of a series of procrastinations I found that we were at home this week with no bread available. Reluctantly, I walked over to the No Frills to get something to tide us over and I brought home this bag of Dimpflmeier.

Now I’ll say that I have never had a Dimpflmeier bread before, maybe they do some amazing rye bread or something. This bread is bad though. I hated it and I’m here to help you make a better decision than I did.

I ate a slice this morning and I felt like I was eating melty plastic that somehow had the texture of bread. It could only be the universe punishing me for failing my mission to patronize our local bakeries. Forgive me universe, I have learned my lesson. I want to pass my message along to everybody else out there: Stay away from Dimpflmeier Farmers’ Gold bread. If you want to eat something bad though this is the thing you should eat.
